key_insight: The band alignment at 2D/3D perovskite interfaces is highly sensitive to surface termination and chemical composition, strongly affecting work function and band offsets.
engineering_relevance: These results help guide interface engineering and passivation choices to improve perovskite solar-cell stability and charge extraction.
method: Hybrid first-principles simulations with hybrid functionals
Atomistic study of (PEA)2PbI4 interfaced with mixed-cation/mixed-halide 3D perovskites
Analysis of work function, electron affinity, macroscopic potential, and band offsets
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary computed band offsets spanning about 0.2–0.7 eV for valence levels and around 0.25 eV for conduction levels, with work function varying by surface cleavage and chemistry.
watch_item: Because the results are preliminary and highly surface-dependent, conclusions may change with different terminations, ionic configurations, or fuller interface models.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
